newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela oil workers demand 300 percent pay rise.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela oil workers demand 300 percent pay rise.

text.p: Venezuela's oilworkers unions proposed a 300 percent pay rise in the opening shot of a five- month negotiation round with the state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela, unionists said on Friday.
Carlos Ortega, representing the 57,000 members of the Fedepetrol and Fetrahidrocarburos unions, said oil workers had not escaped the hardship experienced by other Venezuelans over the past few years.

"We have an explosive situation in the heart of Venezuela's oil workers and this could be detonated, but we don't want to get to that," Ortega told oil company representatives at a meeting in the Employment Ministry.
Claudio Cortes, a Fetrahidrocarburos director, said the workers' proposal included demands for a 300 percent basic salary rise to 360,000 bolivars ($740) per month and greater job security.

"It is said that Venezuela's oil workers are privileged, but we reject this statement completely... Compared to other major oil exporting countries, Venezuelan oil workers see a great inequality," Ortega added.
The minimum monthly salary for Venezuelan workers outside the oil sector was recently increased to 68,000-75,000 bolivars ($140-155).
Guillermo Archila, president of state oil subsidiary Corpoven representing the oil companies at the meeting, said the industry expected a competitive agreement.

"We will have to try our utmost to achieve a collective settlement which will serve as a tool bringing competitive conditions and benefits and to help bring about a new working environment capable of responding to the challenges ahead," he said.
Oil company representatives did not comment on the 300 percent pay claim and said the agreement had to be looked at as a whole.
The two parties are due to come to an agreement covering the period from 1997 to 1999 by November this year.
